paper_metadata.title: The effect of quaternary additions on the microstructures and mechanical properties of orthorhombic Ti2AlNb-based alloys

evidence.quote: In an attempt to enhance the mechanical properties of the orthorhombic Ti2AlNb-based (O-based) alloy, six testing alloys were created by adding the quaternary elements to the O-based alloy.

Most of the cast ingots of the testing alloys (Table 3) were prepared under a high purity argon gas environment using a W-electrode arc melting furnace with a water-cooled Cu crucible. The arc melt was repeated more than 10 times to ensure homogeneity.
Some ingots of Ti–22Al–20Nb–2W were prepared by plasma melting after skull melting.
All of the ingots were forged into 12 mm diameter sticks or roll-milled into 12 mm square bars after being heated at 1150 °C for 30 min.

The values of Q from 327 to 416 kJ mol−1 correspond to those for dislocation-controlled creep [12] and suggest that the creep process is controlled by the dislocation climb.
The O phase can dissolve a great fraction of /p98(bcc phase) stabilizers into solid solution. So it is possible to improve the mechanical properties of the O alloy with solid-solution effects.
The sharp drop in PS at temperatures over 650 or 750 °C as shown in Fig. 2, which was accompanied with the drop in EL, is also likely to be related to the activation of grain boundary sliding.
